title: Meta AI's "Incognito Chat": A Real Privacy Play or Optics?
caption:
Meta AI just dropped "Incognito Chat" in WhatsApp. They promise privacy, but after years of data concerns, is this a genuine shift or just good PR? We break down what it actually means for your conversations.
Tap "BUILD" for the field guide.

slides.headline: "Incognito Chat" for Meta AI in WhatsApp. Is it actually *private*?
slides.sub: Meta's new feature promises privacy. What's the catch?

slides.definition: A new mode for Meta AI within WhatsApp where conversations are not used for training the AI model or retained beyond 30 days.
slides.example: Chatting with Meta AI about sensitive topics without fear of persistent data logging.

slides.title: What Meta *Claims*
slides.body: Meta states Incognito Chat sessions are temporary. They delete after 30 days. Crucially, these interactions won't train future Meta AI models, addressing a major user concern about data usage.

slides.title: What "Incognito" *Doesn't* Mean
bullets: It's for Meta AI chats *only*, not your regular WhatsApp messages.
Meta still collects some metadata (time, participants) for operational purposes.
The feature is *not* end-to-end encrypted like standard WhatsApp chats.
slides.footer: Your data isn't used for training, but it's not invisible.

audiences.body: Those wary of AI using their conversations for model training will find this reassuring, even if it's a limited privacy scope.
Experimenting with Meta AI without contributing to its long-term data pool, useful for sensitive queries or testing.

cards.title: AI Training Exemption
cards.body: Incognito chats are specifically *excluded* from Meta AI's training data.

cards.title: 30-Day Retention
cards.body: Conversations are deleted after 30 days, offering temporary anonymity.

cards.title: AI Chats Only
cards.body: Applies *only* to direct interactions with Meta AI in WhatsApp.

cards.title: Not E2EE
cards.body: Unlike regular WhatsApp, these chats are not end-to-end encrypted.

slides.hook: Meta AI is trying to earn trust. Are you *buying* it?
slides.sub: What's your take on AI privacy?
